objective: Proof and computation. (1) Over a field, a square system of knots (one equation with nonzero coefficients per line) that fails globally has corank 1, so removing any line leaves one degree of freedom: only ties (rigid), at every arity. (2) Over Z_(p^k): a system fails globally exactly when the class of its right-hand side is a nonzero element of every cyclic subgroup generated by a line's unit vector in the cokernel; after removing line L the solutions are a coset of a group of order |coker| times |ann(class of L)|, and a cyclic group leaves only ties. (3) Blurring keeps rigidity; the only proper subgroup of S3^3 (and D_p^3) with full 2-projections is the sign-parity one, so their knots are blurred parity and rigid; simple non-affine Mal'tsev laws on three values have no full-range knots. Checked on random systems over GF(3), GF(5), GF(7), Z4, Z8, Z9, Z25, Z27, the subgroups of S3^3, and a sample of three-element algebras.
status: Proved by RIGID-SELECTION-20261101-001A-P001: over a field every global failure of a knot system has corank 1 and is rigid (only ties after removing a line), at every arity; over Z_(p^k) a failure is global exactly when its class lies in every cyclic subgroup generated by a line's class in the cokernel, the solutions after removing line L form a coset of order |coker| x |ann(class of L)|, and cyclic groups leave only ties; blurring keeps rigidity; S3 and D_p have only sign-parity knots on full ranges, so they are rigid; simple non-affine three-value Mal'tsev laws have no full-range knots
title: Where selection is rigid, and the criterion over Z_(p^k)
